description: Golden eval set for the reconciliation relationship classifier. Each case is a (fragment, existing item) pair with the expected relationship(s). Seeded from the brief's five required cases plus real corrections mined from the live store. expected_any lists acceptable labels (some pairs legitimately admit two).

cases.name: semantic-duplicate-no-shared-words
cases.note: The flagship case: same decision, zero shared keywords. Must NOT be DISTINCT.

item.title: First cohort gets the best models
item.content: Cohort one runs on the strongest available models, no compromise on quality for the founding users.

fragment.text: Piotr personally covers the model cost for cohort one so they always get the top-tier models.

cases.name: real-supersede-50-function-cap
cases.note: A genuine correction from the live store replacing an earlier wrong belief.

item.title: The project is capped at 50 serverless functions
item.content: Deploys fail past 50 functions because the project hit its hard limit of 50 serverless functions; we must delete a function to add one.

fragment.text: CORRECTION: the '50-function cap' is a vercel.json schema limit (the functions object allows at most 50 keys), NOT a limit on deployed functions — the project already deploys 93. Fix is a glob, not deleting endpoints.

cases.name: contradiction-cohort-size
cases.note: Two notes that cannot both be true.

item.title: Cohort one is small and hand-picked
item.content: The first cohort is deliberately under 20 people so each can be onboarded personally.

fragment.text: Cohort one will be around 100 users — we want scale from the start.

cases.name: elaboration-instance-under-principle
cases.note: A specific instance under a general principle — keep apart, link.

item.title: Premium by execution, not by claim
item.content: The product should feel premium through the quality of how it is made, never by stating it is premium in the copy.

fragment.text: On the landing page, we deleted the word 'premium' and instead let the live hypergraph demo carry the feeling of quality.

cases.name: hard-distinct-topically-near
cases.note: The false-merge trap: same domain (cohorts), conceptually separate claims.

item.title: Cohort one gets the best models
item.content: Founding users run on the strongest models available.

fragment.text: Cohort one members will each get a personal onboarding call with Piotr.

cases.name: refinement-adds-detail
cases.note: Same claim, sharper — should version, not duplicate.

item.title: Reconcile before storing
item.content: Incoming fragments should be reconciled against existing items before they become new items.

fragment.text: Reconcile before storing — and a false merge is worse than a false duplicate, so risky relationships like SUPERSEDE need higher confidence than safe ones.

item.title: Tiptap is the editor choice for the Library
item.content: Use the MIT Tiptap core for in-place Markdown editing of Library documents.

fragment.text: Benjamin Franklin treated mistakes as 'errata' — typos to correct in the next edition rather than sources of shame.
